group.passage: Today, purple is everywhere, from school uniforms to sports shirts, and no one thinks of it as special. For most of history, however, wearing purple was a way of announcing that you were rich or powerful. The most famous purple of the ancient world was Tyrian purple, named after the city of Tyre in Phoenicia, where much of it was made. Purple dyes of this kind were being produced as early as 4,000 years ago. Their source was surprising: sea snails known as murex, which produce a mucus that knocks out their prey and keeps enemies away. Dyers left thousands of the snails to dry in the sun, boiled them, and removed the glands that make the mucus, a process that was slow and famously smelly. Because enormous numbers of snails were needed to color even a small piece of cloth, the dye could be worth more than gold. That price turned purple into a badge of rank. From Phoenicia to Greece and Rome, the color came to stand for royalty, and in some places a person caught wearing it without the right social standing could be severely punished, even executed. The color's fate changed in 1856, when William Henry Perkin, an 18-year-old student at the Royal College of Chemistry in London, set out to make quinine, a medicine used against malaria. His experiment failed. Instead of the white crystals he had hoped for, he ended up with a dark, sticky mass. When he tested it further, however, part of it dissolved in alcohol into a brilliant purple liquid that could dye silk. Perkin patented the dye, which became known as mauve. Mauve was cheap to produce and did not fade easily, and it quickly became fashionable. In 1859 the British humor magazine Punch joked that London had caught the mauve measles. Chemists soon created other synthetic dyes in bright shades of red, blue, and yellow, and by about 1860 such dyes were widely available. A color that had once marked kings could now be worn by almost anyone.

translation_zh.text:
今天，紫色隨處可見，從學校制服到運動衫都有，沒有人覺得它特別。然而在歷史上大部分的時間裡，穿紫色是在宣告自己富有或有權勢。
古代最有名的紫色是「泰爾紫」，名稱來自腓尼基的泰爾城，那裡生產了大部分的泰爾紫。這類紫色染料早在四千年前就已經在製造。它的來源出人意料：一種叫骨螺的海螺，牠們分泌的黏液能讓獵物昏迷、讓敵人遠離。染工把成千上萬隻海螺放在太陽下曬乾、加以烹煮，再取出分泌黏液的腺體，過程緩慢，而且出了名地臭。由於即使只染一小塊布也需要數量驚人的海螺，這種染料可能比黃金還值錢。
高昂的價格讓紫色成了身分的標誌。從腓尼基到希臘、羅馬，這個顏色逐漸代表王室；在某些地方，沒有相應社會地位的人若被發現穿紫色，可能遭受嚴懲，甚至被處死。
紫色的命運在 1856 年改變了。那一年，倫敦皇家化學院一名 18 歲的學生威廉・亨利・帕金，著手製造奎寧——一種治療瘧疾的藥。他的實驗失敗了。他沒有得到期待中的白色結晶，而是一團黑色黏稠的東西。然而，當他進一步測試時，其中一部分溶在酒精裡，變成一種亮紫色、能為絲綢染色的液體。帕金為這種染料申請了專利，它後來被稱為「淡紫色」（mauve）。
淡紫色製造成本低、不易褪色，很快就流行起來。1859 年，英國幽默雜誌《笨拙》開玩笑說倫敦染上了「淡紫色麻疹」。化學家很快又做出其他鮮紅、亮藍、明黃的人工染料，到了 1860 年左右，這類染料已經隨處可得。一個曾經代表國王的顏色，如今幾乎人人都能穿。
